#!/usr/local/bin/python3
"""Print a line range of the Semaev 2015 paper, never displaying a redacted line.

Redacted (inclusive) per RD-SEM (blind-inputs.yaml) and RD-SEM-A01
(blind-inputs-amendment-01.yaml). A redacted line is replaced by a marker that
carries its line number only, never its content. Every request is appended to
read_log.txt so the ranges actually displayed are auditable.
"""
import sys, os

PAPER = "/home/user/crypto-autoresearcher/inputs/SEMAEV-2015-310/paper_fulltext.md"
LOG = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "read_log.txt")

RD_SEM = [(1131, 1235)]
RD_SEM_A01 = [(4, 6), (561, 561), (628, 628), (698, 708), (733, 733), (764, 764),
              (780, 780), (900, 926), (994, 1003), (1017, 1017), (1023, 1023),
              (1034, 1037), (1113, 1113), (1236, 1236)]
REDACTED = set()
for a, b in RD_SEM + RD_SEM_A01:
    REDACTED.update(range(a, b + 1))


def main():
    first, last = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
    shown, withheld = [], []
    with open(PAPER, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for no, line in enumerate(fh, start=1):
            if no < first:
                continue
            if no > last:
                break
            if no in REDACTED:
                withheld.append(no)
                print(f"{no:5d}| [REDACTED LINE WITHHELD]")
            else:
                shown.append(no)
                print(f"{no:5d}| {line.rstrip()}")
    with open(LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as lg:
        lg.write(f"request {first}-{last}: displayed {len(shown)} lines; withheld {withheld}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

derivations_AM2.json.ordering_disclosure: The Read tool returned blind-inputs-amendment-01.yaml in full (lines 1-1334) at the start of the task, so its sections transcriptions and changed_definitions were displayed BEFORE these derivations were written. AM-2's ordering was therefore not met; this is recorded as a procedure deviation. The derivations below cite only paper lines; the independence they can claim is limited by that prior exposure.

relation_count_term.result: log2(number of relations collected by the first stage) = k, i.e. the first stage collects 2^k = |V| relations; A(n, m) = k - log2 P(n, m, m, k).

paper_lines.222: 1. Define parameter m and a subset V of Fq of size around q^(1/m).
paper_lines.269: At most |V| relations (7) are necessary on the average.
paper_lines.538-541: V the set of all polynomials in alpha of degree < k = ceil(n/m); a vector space over F2 of dimension k, so |V| = 2^k.
paper_lines.1063-1064: The algorithm complexity is the sum of the complexity of two stages. First collecting a system of <= 2^k, k = ceil(n/m) linear relations (7) and then solving them.
paper_lines.1065-1067: The probability of producing one linear relation by solving at least one system (5) for 2 <= t <= m is at least P(n, m, m, k) ~ 2^(mk-n)/m!, see Section 4.3.
paper_lines.1073-1086: Therefore the complexity of the first stage is 2^k n^(4 omega) / P(n, m, m, k) ~ (m!/2^(mk-n)) 2^k n^(4 omega)   (15)
paper_lines.1088-1091: For omega = 3 that is at most m! 2^(n/m) n^12 (superscripts flattened by the extractor).

relation_count_term.derivation: Equation (15) is (number of relations) x (per-system solving cost) / (probability one system yields a relation). The number of relations is 2^k (lines 1063-1064; consistent with line 269 since |V| = 2^k by lines 538-541). Omitting the per-system solving cost n^(4 omega) as A_of_n_m instructs, log2 of the first-stage cost is A(n, m) = log2(2^k) + log2(1/P(n, m, m, k)) = k - log2 P(n, m, m, k), with t = m.
relation_count_term.full_expression_PF1: A_PF1(n, m) = k - [m k - n - log2(m!)] = n - (m - 1) k + log2(m!). Under KR-A (k = n/m) this is n/m + log2(m!). Under KR-B (k = ceil(n/m)) this is n - (m - 1) ceil(n/m) + log2(m!).
relation_count_term.full_expression_PF2: A_PF2(n, m) = k - log2(1 - exp(-2^(m k - n)/m!)). Under KR-A this is n/m - log2(1 - exp(-1/m!)). Under KR-B this is ceil(n/m) - log2(1 - exp(-2^(m ceil(n/m) - n)/m!)).

N5.result: N5(n, t, k) = (t - 2) n + t k Boolean variables; at t = m, N5 = (m - 2) n + m k.

paper_lines.228-238: System (5): S3(u1, x1, x2) = 0; S3(ui, ui+1, xi+2) = 0, 1 <= i <= t - 3; S3(ut-2, xt, RX) = 0, in unknowns x1..xt in V and u1..ut-2 in Fq.
paper_lines.538-541: V has dimension k over F2, so each xi contributes k Boolean coordinates; each ui in F_(2^n) contributes n.
paper_lines.368-372: The system (5) for t = m is equivalent to a system of (m - 1)n multivariate equations in (m - 2)n + km ~ (m - 1)n variables in Fp.
paper_lines.611-613: The system consists of n(t - 1) coordinate equations in n(t - 2) + kt variables and n(t - 2) + kt field equations are added.

N5.derivation: Weil descent of system (5) writes each of the t - 2 unknowns ui in F_(2^n) as n Boolean coordinates and each of the t unknowns xi in V as k Boolean coordinates (V of dimension k). The paper states the count explicitly at lines 611-613 for general t and at lines 368-372 for t = m.
N5.integer_status: Under KR-B k = ceil(n/m) is an integer, so N5 is an integer. Under KR-A k = n/m and m k = n exactly, so N5 = (m - 1) n is an integer as well; unrounded, nearest and ceiled agree under both readings. Line 372 itself notes (m - 2)n + km ~ (m - 1)n. The paper's own k is the integer ceil(n/m) (lines 360, 541, 602-603, 617, 623, 1064), so its text supports the KR-B count.
